analysis.reason: The paper develops NuSrcAgent, an open-source LLM AI agent that translates natural-language instructions into unbinned likelihood analyses on public IceCube data for high-energy neutrino point sources and source populations (e.g., NGC 1068, magnetars, and blazar flares).
analysis.reading_entry: II Neutrino Data and Likelihood Formulation
analysis.problem: Identifying the astrophysical origins of the diffuse high-energy cosmic neutrino flux requires complex likelihood analyses over years of data, where non-expert workflows are error-prone and existing background energy PDFs (e.g., SkyLLH v1) leave residual count offsets that accumulate spurious signals in source-stacking analyses.
analysis.method: The framework executes unbinned extended likelihood analyses using $\mathcal{L}(n,\boldsymbol{\theta})=\prod_{k}\prod_{i=1}^{N_{k}}[\frac{nf_{k}(\boldsymbol{\theta})}{N_{k}}\mathcal{S}_{i}^{k}(\boldsymbol{\theta})+(1-\frac{nf_{k}(\boldsymbol{\theta})}{N_{k}})\mathcal{B}_{i}^{k}]$ and test statistic $\mathrm{TS}=2\ln[\mathcal{L}(\widehat{n},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}})/\mathcal{L}(0)]$, where signal and background factorize into spatial, energy, and temporal PDFs ($\mathcal{S}_{ij}^{k}=S_{ij,\mathrm{spatial}}^{k}S_{ij,\mathrm{energy}}^{k}S_{ij,\mathrm{temporal}}^{k}$). An upgraded v3 background PDF applies an adaptive sliding-window algorithm across declination and energy bins to eliminate residuals.
limits: Confidence levels of both the upper limits and flux-measurement intervals rely on asymptotic approximations unless calibrated with computational background/signal injection trials.
citation_leads: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches: “The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data”
IV Background PDFs: “leave residuals between the observed and predicted event counts in energy-proxy bins”
II Neutrino Data and Likelihood Formulation: “The parameter $n$ is the total expected signal count across all detector phases”
V.3 Time-integrated stacking analysis: magnetars: “gives a flux upper limit consistent with the thesis within the Monte Carlo uncertainty.”
V.3 Time-integrated stacking analysis: magnetars: “With v3 background PDFs, NuSrcAgent reproduces the published spectral index to its quoted precision”
B.3 Upper limits and flux measurements: “The confidence levels of both the upper limits and flux-measurement intervals rely on asymptotic approximations.”
analysis.research_progress: NuSrcAgent automates end-to-end neutrino point-source and stacking pipelines, integrating external GitHub spectral models and Neyman upper-limit construction while curing spurious stacking signals by reducing false test statistics from $\mathrm{TS}=30\text{--}75$ (v1) down to $\mathrm{TS}=0\text{--}9$ (v3) across random isotropic catalogs.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a multi-year low-frequency (102-198 MHz) study of Crab giant pulses using I-LOFAR, investigating the dynamic correlation between dispersion measure (DM) and scattering timescales as probes of plasma turbulence in the Crab Nebula.
analysis.result: Dispersive delay scales as $\Delta t \propto \mathrm{DM}\,\nu^{-2}$ across the $102.23\text{--}197.55\text{ MHz}$ band, alongside scattering broadening $\tau(f) = \tau_{150}[f/150~\mathrm{MHz}]^\alpha$. Measured $\mathrm{DM}$ and $\tau$ exhibit strong positive correlation ($r = 0.71 \pm 0.04$, $\rho = 0.78 \pm 0.04$ for the thin screen model), peaking at $r \approx 0.48\text{--}0.49$ after removing long-term trends at a sliding window of $W \approx 125\text{--}190~\mathrm{d}$ with zero lag, alongside an isolated nebula filament crossing event with $\Delta\mathrm{DM} \approx 0.02~\mathrm{pc~cm^{-3}}$.
analysis.problem: Low-frequency radio timing and DM determination of giant pulses are severely degenerated by intense scattering broadening, while solar wind electron density fluctuations ($n \propto r^{-2}$) are masked by large intrinsic DM variations within the Crab Nebula.
analysis.method: Giant pulse searching was conducted via TransientX on 8-bit filterbanks, followed by coherent metric optimization with DM_phase maximizing $S(\mathrm{DM}) = \sum_f w(f) P(f;\mathrm{DM})$ on phase-normalized spectra, and scattering tail fitting across $9.53~\mathrm{MHz}$ subbands using modified thin-screen and thick-screen models evaluated by the Akaike Information Criterion.
assumptions: Dispersive pulse delay scales strictly as $\Delta t \propto \nu^{-2}$ while the scattering timescale across subbands follows $\tau(f) \propto f^\alpha$.
limits: Scattering pulse broadening at low frequencies induces apparent DM shifts and limits single giant pulse DM precision, while Crab Nebula intrinsic DM variations exceed the solar wind signal ($10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-4}~\mathrm{pc~cm^{-3}}$).
citation_leads: 3.2 Identifying Pulses: “To reduce computational cost, the search was performed on 8-bit filterbanks rather than 32-bit.”

3.3 Correcting the DM: “Due to the large amount of scattering present at lower frequencies, traditional boxcar single-pulse searches can often over or underestimate the DM as they simply maximise S/N over a reasonably coarse search grid in DM and pulse width.”

4.3 Scattering: “The lower the observing frequency, the smaller the DM uncertainty, since the dispersive delay across a fixed bandwidth scales as $\sim f^{-2}$, in theory improving the accuracy of the determined DM.”
4.5 Implications on the Solar Wind: “The variations in DM caused by the Crab Nebula are too large to measure temporal variations in electron content caused by the solar wind.”
analysis.research_progress: Constrained multi-year co-evolution of $\mathrm{DM}$ and scattering $\tau$ on month-scale baselines for Crab giant pulses at metric wavelengths, and established limits on disentangling turbulent nebula filament crossings from solar wind variations.

analysis.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch spectropolarimetry and 3D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of the Type Ibn supernova SN 2025kzr, offering constraints on circumstellar interaction geometry and ejecta-CSM alignment.
analysis.result: The optical spectrum displays $\mathrm{He\ I}$ emission with $\mathrm{FWHM} \sim 1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, confirming strong ejecta-CSM interaction. After subtracting the interstellar polarization ($Q_{\mathrm{ISP}} = 0.154\% \pm 0.145\%, U_{\mathrm{ISP}} = 0.396\% \pm 0.173\%$, $P_{\mathrm{ISP}} \approx 0.43\%$, $\theta_{\mathrm{ISP}} \approx 34^\circ$), the intrinsic continuum polarization reaches $P = 0.462\% \pm 0.071\%$ at $+8.0\ \mathrm{d}$ with $(Q_{\mathrm{Cont}}, U_{\mathrm{Cont}}) = (0.242\% \pm 0.076\%, -0.394\% \pm 0.067\%)$, subsequently declining to $P = 0.042\% \pm 0.071\%$ at $+12\ \mathrm{d}$ and consistent with zero by $+21\ \mathrm{d}$. The polarization vector traces an evolving loop in the $Q-U$ plane: from near zero at $4.9\ \mathrm{d}$ to $(Q, U) \approx (0.21\%, -0.34\%)$ at $8.0\ \mathrm{d}$, rotating to $(0.49\%, 0.32\%)$ at $10.9\ \mathrm{d}$. The $\mathrm{He\ I}\ \lambda 5876$ line polarization aligns with a dominant axis angle $\theta_{\mathrm{DA}} = (-45.6^{+15.6}_{-15.5})^\circ$. The polarization trajectory is reproduced by an interaction between a prolate ejecta ($A_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.25, \theta_{\mathrm{ej}} = +8^\circ$) and an oblate CSM ($A_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 1.20, \theta_{\mathrm{CSM}} = -25^\circ$) accompanied by anisotropic surface luminance $L_{\mathrm{iso}}/L_{\mathrm{iso,max}}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2. Hydrodynamic Model and Q − U Evolution
analysis.problem: Unraveling the multi-dimensional geometry and alignment of the dense helium-rich CSM and supernova ejecta in Type Ibn SN 2025kzr, breaking the geometric degeneracies inherent to 1D light curve models (e.g., $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}} \propto r^{-3}$) and flux spectra.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch spectropolarimetry using VLT/FORS2 (300V grism, $3500\text{--}9200\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$, $R \approx 440$) at $+8.0, +25.0, +34.0\ \mathrm{d}$ combined with $V$-band imaging polarimetry across 5–34 days. ISP was determined from late-time iron-group element phases. 3D gray radiation-hydrodynamics simulations were performed using Athena++ for a broken power-law prolate ejecta ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.85\ M_\odot, E_{\mathrm{kin}} = 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}, \delta=1, m=10, v_{\mathrm{br}} = 8.81 \times 10^8\ \mathrm{cm\ s^{-1}}$) colliding with an oblate broken-density CSM ($s_1=0.5, s_2=30, s_3=2$), followed by 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer in MCPol tracking $2 \times 10^6$ photon packets.
assumptions: The CSM is modeled as an oblate ellipsoid with axial ratio $A_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 1.20$, while the SN ejecta is modeled as a prolate ellipsoid with $A_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.25$.
limits: Smooth axisymmetric ellipsoidal geometries with post-processed electron scattering introduce parameter degeneracies among geometry, viewing angle, optical depth, and ISP.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Time-variable ejecta-CSM geometry and the model continuum polarization. Panel A: Schematic of the interaction region that spans the transition from CSM-interaction-dominated to CDS-dominated phases (see Section III.2 ) as seen perpendicular to the $x$ – $z$ plane. At $\sim$ 0–6 d, the forward shock (solid red) is embedded in the optically thick, oblate CSM (blue) and lies inside the $\tau=1$ surface (dashed orange). At $\sim$ 7–11 d, the forward shock approaches the outer, optically thinner part of the dense CSM. After $\sim$ 11 d, the shock has swept through the dense CSM, the CDS has formed between the forward and reverse shocks, and the $\tau=1$ surface lies within the CDS at some angles. The long axes of the prolate SN ejecta (red arrow) and the oblate CSM (blue arrow) are misaligned, with inclinations $\theta_{\rm ej}$ and $\theta_{\rm CSM}$ (Section IV ). The schematic is not to scale. Panel B: Model continuum polarization $P$ of the oblate, CSM-dominated phase as a function of the axis ratio $A_{\rm oblate}=a/c$, where $a$ and $c$ are the equatorial and polar semiaxes. Blue, orange, and green dashed curves show photon packets injected at electron-scattering optical depths of $\tau=1$, 2, and 3, respectively. Gray-shaded band shows the observed, ISP-corrected and bias-corrected polarization and its $1\sigma$ uncertainty at 4.9 d and 8d, respectively. Panel C: Same as Panel B but for the prolate, CDS-dominated phase as a function of $A_{\rm prolate}=c/a$, compared with the observation at 10.9 d. Panels B and C show that polarization increases with asphericity and decreases with injection depth.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Presents the geometric framework of the interaction region across the transition from an oblate CSM-dominated phase to a prolate CDS-dominated phase with misaligned symmetry axes ($\theta_{\rm ej}$ and $\theta_{\rm CSM}$), alongside theoretical continuum polarization curves $P$ modeled as functions of axis ratios ($A_{\rm oblate}=a/c$, $A_{\rm prolate}=c/a$) and electron-scattering optical depth $\tau = 1, 2, 3$.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Hydrodynamic structure, emitting-surface brightness, and polarization evolution of the model at 5, 8, and 11 d. Panel A: Density maps in the $x$ – $z$ plane. Colors show $\log_{10}(\rho/\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}})$. The dark-green solid, yellow dashed, and blue dash-dotted curves denote the forward shock, the $\tau=1$ surface, and the $\rho=10^{-16}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ contour tracing the CSM geometry, respectively. Panel B: Normalized brightness distributions of the emitting surfaces viewed from the $-y$ direction. The 5 d surface is the shock surface, whereas the 8 and 11 d surfaces are defined by $\tau=1$. Colors indicate $L_{\rm iso}/L_{\rm iso,max}$, normalized independently at each epoch. Panel C: Comparison between the modeled and ISP-corrected observed Stokes parameters in the $Q-U$ plane. Colored diamonds show the $+y$ model predictions at 5, 8, and 11 d; open circles present the observations at 4.9, 8.0, and 10.9 d. The black solid curve connects the model epochs, and dotted segments illustrate the model–observation offsets. Error bars indicate $1\sigma$ uncertainties, including Monte Carlo uncertainties for the model and measurement uncertainties for the observations.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: Displays the 2D hydrodynamic density structure $\log_{10}(\rho/\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}})$ showing forward shock and $\tau=1$ surfaces, the normalized emitting surface brightness $L_{\rm iso}/L_{\rm iso,max}$ at 5, 8, and 11 d, and the direct comparison between Monte Carlo model trajectories and observed Stokes parameters in the $Q-U$ plane across 4.9, 8.0, and 10.9 d.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates collisional neutrino-flavor instability under realistic conditions of forward-peaked angular anisotropy, energy dependence, and spatial inhomogeneity relevant to core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers.
analysis.result: For near/gapless modes dominant at low collisional rates ($\bar{R}_{0}=10^{-5}$), the maximum growth rate reaches $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega \sim 9.0\times 10^{-4}$ at $(\mathrm{Re}\,\omega, k) \simeq (3.7\times 10^{-4}, 4.3\times 10^{-4})$. The flavor survival probability asymptotically tends to flavor equipartition $P_{ee} = \frac{1}{2}(P_{0}+P_{3})/P_{0} \simeq \frac{1}{2}(1+\|\bm{P}\|/P_{0})$ governed by polarization vector decoherence $\mathrm{d}_{t}\|\bm{P}\|^{2} \propto -R_{\mathrm{EA}}|\rho_{ex}|^{2} \propto -R_{\mathrm{EA}}/(1+R_{\mathrm{EA}}^{2})$, while collisional decoherence suppresses spatial cascading and prevents strong spatial inhomogeneity.
analysis.problem: Previous investigations of collisional flavor conversion were largely confined to isotropic, monoenergetic, and spatially homogeneous neutrino gases, leaving unresolved how forward-peaked angular anisotropy and spatial mode coupling interact with collisional decoherence in semitransparent decoupling layers ($\rho \sim 10^{10-12}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$).
analysis.method: The authors solve 1D quantum kinetic equations $\left(p^{\mu}\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{\mu}}-\Gamma^{j}_{\alpha\beta}p^{\alpha}p^{\beta}\frac{\partial}{\partial p^{j}}\right)\overset{\scriptscriptstyle(-)}{\rho}=-\mathrm{i}\left[\overset{\scriptscriptstyle(-)}{\mathcal{H}}_{\mathrm{osc}},\,\overset{\scriptscriptstyle(-)}{\rho}\right]+\mathcal{C}\left[\overset{\scriptscriptstyle(-)}{\rho}\right]$ using the GANTS-QK code in a 1D box ($L_z = 1000, N_z = 1000$), combined with linear dispersion relation analysis $\Pi^{\mu\nu}(\omega,\bm{k})\tilde{a}_{\nu}=0$ with angular moment integrals $I_{n}\equiv\int\mathrm{d}\Gamma\,G_{ex}\frac{v^{n}}{v\cdot k+\mathrm{i}R_{\mathrm{EA}}}$ and first-order collisional corrections $\delta\omega_{\mathrm{col}}=\mathrm{i}\,C(\omega_{0})/\mathcal{D}'(\omega_{0})+\mathcal{O}(R_{\mathrm{EA}}^{2})$.
citation_leads: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence: “additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability.”
III Collisional Modes: “explore the unstable branch responsible for flavor instabilities and the corresponding eigenvectors”
IV.1 Near/Gapless mode dominant case: “the flavor coherence is restored even though neutrinos have undergone decoherence due to collisions.”
V Summary and Conclusions: “occurrence of secondary flavor growth after the initial flavor conversion and decoherence.”
analysis.research_progress: Uncovers that post-CFC states can destabilize previously damped far/gapped branches to trigger secondary flavor growth, demonstrating that competition between flavor depolarization and collisional decoherence sets the asymptotic state rather than unrestrained spatial cascading.

analysis.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch broadband X-ray spectral and timing observations of the atoll-type neutron star low-mass X-ray binary GX 9+9, placing quantitative physical constraints on the boundary layer size, accretion disk truncation, and compact object magnetic field.
analysis.result: Broadband spectral fits show GX 9+9 remains in a soft banana state with bolometric luminosity $L_{\rm bol} \sim 0.29\text{--}0.33~L_{\rm Edd}$, where Comptonization accounts for only $\sim 6\text{--}12\%$ of the flux. The neutron star boundary layer radial extent is determined to be $R_{\rm BL} \sim 16.6\text{--}17.3\text{ km}$ (corresponding to $\sim 8\text{--}8.4~r_{\rm g}$ for $M = 1.4~M_\odot$), and assuming disk truncation at the magnetospheric radius yields a magnetic dipole moment $\mu \lesssim 3\times 10^{28}\text{ G cm}^3$ and surface magnetic field upper limit $B \lesssim 3\times 10^{10}\text{ G}$.
analysis.problem: Constraining the inner accretion geometry, the physical origin of disk truncation, and the radial extent of the boundary layer in the bright, persistently soft atoll NS-LMXB GX 9+9 using broadband X-ray spectroscopy and timing.
analysis.method: Joint broadband spectral modeling ($0.7\text{--}40\text{ keV}$) using NICER, NuSTAR, and MAXI data with the model $\mathrm{plabs} \times \mathrm{tbabs}(\mathrm{diskbb} + \mathrm{thcomp} \times \mathrm{bbody} + \mathrm{relxillNs})$, combined with Fourier-based complex cross-power density spectral (CPDS) timing analysis of NuSTAR FPMA and FPMB light curves.

analysis.reason: This work directly addresses the progenitor channels of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by testing whether FRBs track cosmic star formation history promptly or with a multi-gigayear delay time distribution.
analysis.result: When marginalizing over fluence calibration systematics and fitting the dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}$) distribution alone, both CHIME catalogs reveal a significant cosmological time delay: Catalog 1 yields $t_{d}=3.90^{+0.50}_{-0.41}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.99^{+0.01}_{-0.24}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, while Catalog 2 yields $t_{d}=3.53^{+0.11}_{-0.10}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.82^{+0.15}_{-0.14}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, resolving the apparent $t_d \sim 0$ result that arises from instrumental $\mathrm{S/N}$--fluence mapping biases.
analysis.problem: Whether FRB occurrence rates follow prompt core-collapse supernova magnetar channels or delayed compact binary mergers, and how systematic uncertainties in telescope beam attenuation and fluence threshold mapping bias delay time inference in forward modeling.
analysis.method: Forward modeling using a two-dimensional binning scheme over $\mathrm{S/N}$ and $\mathrm{DM}$ with synthetic injection samples, Poisson likelihood $\ln\mathcal{L}\propto\sum_{i,j}[n_{ij}\ln\zeta_{ij}-\zeta_{ij}]$, and an intrinsic burst energy distribution parameterized by a Schechter function $P(E)\propto\frac{1}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\left(\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)^{\gamma}\exp\left(-\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)$ convolved with cosmic SFR and Gaussian DTD.

analysis.reason: This survey paper provides empirical constraints on the occurrence and physics of relativistic jets in high-redshift ($z \ge 4$) QSOs using EMU radio data, testing orientation and Doppler beaming models.
analysis.result: EMU detects $124/808$ ($15\%$) of $z \ge 4$ QSOs, with detection fractions rising to $\sim 37\%$ at the optically bright end ($\mathrm{mag}_{\rm drop} \sim 18$). The radio-loud fraction ($R > 10$) remains stable at $8 \pm 1\%$. High radio powers of $P_{5\,\mathrm{GHz}} = 5\times 10^{24}\text{--}5\times 10^{27}\,\mathrm{W}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1}$ demonstrate that many formally radio-quiet sources are misaligned jetted systems viewed at angles $\theta \sim 20^\circ\text{--}40^\circ$, including rare candidate blazars at $z > 6$ with $R > 300$.
analysis.problem: Investigating whether high-redshift radio-quiet ($R < 10$) QSOs genuinely lack relativistic jets or if traditional radio loudness criteria fail due to Doppler de-beaming and suppressed extended lobe emission in the early Universe.
analysis.method: Cross-matching $808$ optically confirmed $z \ge 4$ QSOs with ASKAP EMU survey data at $0.943\,\mathrm{GHz}$ using a $6.4''$ positional tolerance. Relativistic beaming is modeled as $P^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}}(\theta) = \mathcal{P}^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}}\delta^p(\theta)$ with Doppler factor $\delta(\theta) = [\Gamma(1 - \beta\cos\theta)]^{-1}$ ($p = 3.3$, $\Gamma = 10$), predicting radio loudness $R(\theta) = R(0)[(\delta^p(\theta) + 1/f_5)/(\delta^p(0) + 1/f_5)]$ where $f_5 = \mathcal{P}^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}} / \mathcal{P}^{\rm ext}_{5{\rm GHz}} \sim 0.1\text{--}1$.
assumptions: Positional offsets follow Gaussian distributions with $\sigma_{\Delta\alpha,\Delta\delta} \approx 2.1''$, yielding $\sim 99\%$ completeness at a $6.4''$ tolerance radius.
limits: The $\sim 15''$ angular resolution of EMU corresponds to $\sim 80\text{--}100\,\mathrm{kpc}$ at $z=4\text{--}6.6$, leaving sources unresolved and preventing morphological separation of cores and extended lobes without VLBI.

3 Radio-emitting QSOs at z$>$5.5: “they are either confirmed or good candidate blazars.”

6 Summary and conclusions: “most of these high-z QSOs are characterized by a weak extended emission.”
analysis.research_progress: Reveals that the radio-loud parameter $R$ significantly underestimates the true fraction of relativistic jets at $z > 4$, as severe CMB inverse Compton losses ($U_{\rm CMB} \propto (1+z)^4$) and young dynamical stages suppress extended emission.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates unexplained near-horizon RFI observed in air shower radio arrays (e.g., AERA, OVRO-LWA, BEACON, GRAND), proposing cloud reflections of anthropogenic emissions as the underlying physical mechanism.
analysis.result: Under bistatic forward-scattering geometry at grazing elevation ($\epsilon = 5^\circ$, bistatic angle $\theta = 170^\circ$), the simulated peak instantaneous radar cross section of a cloud reaches $\sigma \sim 0.1\ \mathrm{m}^2$ ($-10\ \mathrm{dBsm}$), demonstrating that cloud reflection of ground-based transmitters can produce detectable near-horizon pulses.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.4 The radar cross section from a cloud
analysis.problem: Radio detection of cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy neutrinos is contaminated by sporadic, near-horizon ($10^\circ\text{--}20^\circ$ elevation) radio frequency interference (RFI) that cannot be eliminated by conventional horizon cuts.
analysis.method: The study develops a passive radar scattering framework (MARES), dividing a cloud into cubic cells of size $L_c \simeq 1.6d$ with Gaussian positional jitter $\delta = L_c/3$ to suppress artificial Bragg resonances, and computes single-droplet Rayleigh scattering (dielectric factor $|K_{\mathrm{water}}|^2 \approx 0.93$) and coherent cell radar cross section (RCS).
assumptions: Water droplets at MHz frequencies satisfy the Rayleigh scattering limit $a \ll \lambda$ and act as coherent dielectric scatterers with $|K_{\mathrm{water}}|^2 \approx 0.93$.
limits: The model adopts first-order approximations assuming monodisperse droplet sizes and idealized cloud geometry without accounting for full atmospheric turbulence or multipath propagation.

analysis.reason: This paper presents Chandra sub-arcsecond imaging of the middle-aged supernova remnant G22.7$-$0.2 interacting with molecular clouds, confirming spatial extension in crushed cloud clumps (CCCs) powered by non-thermal bremsstrahlung from low-energy cosmic rays.
analysis.result: Chandra ACIS-I PSF modeling and deconvolution resolve spatial extension in CCC candidates at $d \sim 4.4\text{--}4.7\ \mathrm{kpc}$: N2 displays significant extension with $R_{90} = 2.35^{\prime\prime}$ (physical radius $r \sim 0.052\pm 0.002\ \mathrm{pc}$), N1 exhibits marginal extension with $R_{90} = 0.82^{\prime\prime}$ ($r \sim 0.018\pm 0.0006\ \mathrm{pc}$), while N3 is point-like ($R_{90} = 0.31^{\prime\prime}$). N2's hard spectrum (photon index $\Gamma = 1.2^{+0.4}_{-0.4}$) and uniform-sphere mass ($M \approx 0.6\ M_\odot$ at shock-compressed density $n_{\mathrm{H}} \sim 3\times 10^4\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$) match non-thermal bremsstrahlung (NTB, predicted $\Gamma \simeq 1$), whereas N1 ($\\Gamma = 2.1^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$, $M \approx 0.03\ M_\odot$) favors a high-density synchrotron hot spot.
analysis.reading_entry: V.1 Characterizing the CCC Candidates Discovered in the Chandra Survey
analysis.problem: Observational constraints on the cloud clump mass function (CMF, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\ln M \propto M^{-\alpha}$) at the theoretical minimum scale $r \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\ \mathrm{pc}$ have been lacking due to spatial resolution limits, leaving the spatial extent and dominant non-thermal emission mechanism (synchrotron vs. non-thermal bremsstrahlung) of hard X-ray ($>10\ \mathrm{keV}$) sources in middle-aged SNRs unresolved.
analysis.method: Analyzed Chandra ACIS-I observations ($58.05\ \mathrm{ks}$ total exposure) using `wavdetect` in $0.5\text{--}7.0\ \mathrm{keV}$, simulated local PSFs via ChaRT v2 and MARX 5.5.3 using absorbed power-law spectral models, fitted radial profiles with a Moffat function $\mathrm{Flux\ density} = \mathrm{ampl}\times [1 + ((x - x_{\mathrm{pos}})/r_0)^2]^{0.5 - 3\beta}$, deconvolved source radial models from PSF models to obtain the 90% encircled flux radius $R_{90}$, and modeled forward dust-scattering halos with differential cross-section $\frac{\mathrm{d}\sigma_{\mathrm{sca}}}{\mathrm{d}\Omega} \propto a^6 \exp[-0.4575 E^2 a^2 \theta_{\mathrm{sca}}^2]$.
limits: CCCs have subtle radial extents ($r \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\ \mathrm{pc}$) that can easily be mistaken for point-like sources without sub-arcsecond PSF deconvolution.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a large-scale statistical identification and multi-frequency geometric modeling of 586 curved parsec-scale relativistic jets in AGN, providing systematic observational constraints on relativistic jet propagation, precession mechanisms, and supermassive black hole binary or accretion disc dynamics.
analysis.result: Among 7,927 resolved AGN sources, 586 show reliable curvature with bending rate $|K|$ increasing at higher frequencies, tracing stronger deflection in the innermost jet. Linear helical modeling gives a mean curvature $K^{-1}_{\rm mean} = 109^{\circ}/{\rm mas}$, corresponding to inferred precession periods $P \sim 10\text{--}10^{4}~{\rm yr}$ (logarithmic mean $218.8~{\rm yr}$). For binary black hole models, disk tidal precession $P_{\rm td} \approx 6.5 \times 10^{2} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{3} (R_{d}/10^{4} r_{g})^{-3/2}~{\rm yr}$ matches observations much better than spin geodetic precession $P_{\rm geo} \approx 2.6 \times 10^{8} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{5/2}~{\rm yr}$, while tilted thick disc Lense-Thirring precession $P_{\rm BH, spin, thick} \approx 24.7 s^{-1} M_{8} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{g})^{3} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{\rm i})^{1/2}~{\rm yr}$ naturally reproduces the observed range of $10^{1\text{--}5}~{\rm yr}$.
analysis.problem: Determining the physical origins of parsec-scale relativistic jet bending in active galaxies, specifically distinguishing between geometric precession (induced by supermassive binary black hole orbits or Bardeen-Petterson/Lense-Thirring disc warping) and plasma dynamical instabilities (Kelvin-Helmholtz helical modes).
analysis.method: Filtered 123,456 Astrogeo VLBI images (1.2–86 GHz) down to 63,879 images of 7,927 resolved sources using 2D Gaussian subtraction with threshold $\sigma_{\rm crit} = 5.5\sigma_{\rm map}$. analysis.reason: This paper presents IXPE X-ray polarization constraints on the western lobe of microquasar SS 433, setting a 99% confidence upper limit of $\mathrm{PD} < 32\%$. analysis.result: IXPE observations reveal non-detection of X-ray polarization in the western lobe of SS 433, with best-fit Stokes parameters $Q = -0.01 \pm 0.12$ and $U = 0.01 \pm 0.13$, equivalent to $\mathrm{PD} = 1.4\% \pm 12.5\%$ and a 99% confidence upper limit of $\mathrm{PD} < 32\%$. The polarization degree is significantly lower than that of the eastern lobe ($\mathrm{PD} \approx 49\%\text{--}50\%$) at 99.5% ($2.8\sigma$) confidence, despite both lobes having comparable non-thermal photon indices ($\Gamma \approx 1.6$) and magnetic field strengths ($B \approx 10\text{--}15\,\mu\mathrm{G}$).
analysis.problem: Investigating whether the western lobe of SS 433 exhibits high X-ray polarization and ordered magnetic fields aligned with the jet direction, comparable to the eastern lobe where synchrotron emission shows high polarization and well-ordered magnetic fields.
analysis.method: Weighted spectropolarimetric analysis combining spatial, spectral, and particle character weights using leakagelib in the $2\text{--}5.5\,\mathrm{keV}$ band on IXPE observations (exposure $> 9.6 \times 10^5\,\mathrm{s}$ per DU), accounting for Chandra-derived astrophysical background and unabsorbed power-law instrumental background ($\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} = 161/147$) with a $1/\mathrm{PD}$ prior to correct for Ricean bias.

analysis.reason: J1912-4410 is only the second known white dwarf pulsar, providing a critical laboratory to test compact object spin-down power and magnetospheric non-thermal emission mechanisms. Measuring its spin-down rate directly tests whether the system is purely rotationally powered or aided by accretion.
analysis.problem: Determining whether the multi-wavelength pulsed non-thermal emission of the white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410 is powered solely by rotational spin-down or assisted by accretion, and testing the viability of the unipolar synchronar magnetospheric interaction model.
analysis.method: Multi-band ($u, g, r, i$) high-speed time-series photometry obtained with ULTRACAM over 28 nights was reduced with HiPERCAM. Pulse arrival times were derived via cross-correlation with a Gaussian template (optimal width $\sigma = 29.3\,\mathrm{s}$ in $g$). Orbital modulation and timing residuals were disentangled using a 10-term Fourier series and iteratively fitted to a quadratic ephemeris $T_{\rm max} = T_0 + P_{\rm spin} E + \frac{1}{2} P_{\rm spin} \dot{P}_{\rm spin} E^2$ with MCMC parameter estimation.
limits: Pulse arrival times in the $i$-band deviate from the consistent $u, g, r$ ephemeris, possibly due to filter-dependent emission heights or chromatic phase offsets
citation_leads: Determining the Spin-down of the White Dwarf in J191213.72-441045.1 using Optical Time-Series Photometry: “J191213.72-441045.1 (J1912-4410) is the second white dwarf pulsar to be discovered.”

analysis.research_progress: Provides the first robust measurement of the spin-down rate $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = 4.13(8) \times 10^{-12}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and spin-down luminosity $\dot{E}_{\rm rot} = 9^{+6}_{-5} \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{W}$ for the second white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410, showing that WD pulsars are a heterogeneous class and conclusively ruling out the synchronar model ($B \ge 110 \pm 50\,\mathrm{MG}$ vs. empirical upper limit $B \lesssim 50\,\mathrm{MG}$).

analysis.reason: This paper presents observational sensitivity forecasts and theoretical frameworks for measuring the flavor composition of Galactic and extragalactic high-energy neutrinos using eight neutrino telescopes, enabling tests of cosmic-ray hadronic production mechanisms, source magnetic fields, and neutrino decay.
analysis.result: With eight neutrino telescopes, the source electron flavor fraction $f_{e,{\rm S}}$ for the inner Galactic plane can be measured to $27\%$ precision at $68\%$ C.L., distinguishing pion decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1/3$) from muon damping ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=0$) and neutron decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1$) at $>95\%$ C.L. In extragalactic sources, muon synchrotron cooling above $E_{c} \approx E_{c,\mu}/3$ with $E_{c,\mu} \simeq 6\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$ can be detected at $\ge 3\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 11\text{ kG}$ ($5\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 22\text{ kG}$), while neutrino invisible decay lifetime-to-mass ratio can be probed up to $\tau/m \sim 1.5\times 10^4\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ at $2\sigma$.
analysis.reading_entry: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
analysis.problem: High-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way have an unknown flavor composition $(f_{e}, f_{\mu}, f_{\tau})$ and production origin (diffuse interstellar $pp$ collisions versus unresolved discrete sources), and existing facilities lack the sensitivity to distinguish emission mechanisms, detect muon synchrotron cooling in magnetized environments, or constrain neutrino decay against extragalactic baselines.
analysis.method: The analysis uses a frequentist profile likelihood method based on Poisson event rates and Wilks' theorem across eight neutrino telescopes (IceCube, KM3NeT/ARCA, Baikal-GVD, P-ONE, TRIDENT, NEON, HUNT, IceCube-Gen2). The framework models detector tracks and cascades, computes atmospheric backgrounds using MCEq with Sibyll-2.3d and nuVeto self-veto, incorporates muon synchrotron cooling with critical cutoff $E_{c} \simeq 2\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$, and folds in standard averaged neutrino oscillations $f_{\beta,\oplus} = \sum_{\alpha} P_{\alpha\beta} f_{\alpha,{\rm S}}$.
assumptions: Neutrinos in standard hadronuclear environments are produced via charged pion decay chains giving source flavor ratios $(f_{e,{\rm S}}, f_{\mu,{\rm S}}, f_{\tau,{\rm S}}) = (1/3, 2/3, 0)$ without initial tau neutrinos.
limits: Muon synchrotron cooling produces observable spectral/flavor suppression only in magnetized environments with $B \gtrsim 10^4\text{ G}$ where $E_c \lesssim 100\text{ TeV}$.
citation_leads: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way: “The significance with which the fractions are told apart grows in proportion to their difference, whatever their values.”
Appendix A Cooling in the extragalactic sources: “A muon in a magnetic field $B$ loses energy by synchrotron radiation faster than it decays above the energy”
analysis.research_progress: The study demonstrates that multi-telescope arrays scale flavor discrimination significance linearly with fraction difference $|\Delta f_{e,{\rm S}}|$, improving the constraint on Galactic $f_{e,{\rm S}}$ from $88\%$ with current facilities to $27\%$, breaking degeneracies between pion decay and muon-damped regimes, and extending neutrino decay limits by over an order of magnitude.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Flavor composition of the high-energy neutrinos along the Galactic plane and from outside it. Forecast measurements of the composition at Earth in IceCube’s three segments of the plane and of the extragalactic flux, all fitted together with every systematic uncertainty. The segments span ranges of Galactic longitude, $l$, at Galactic latitudes $|b| [ 9 ] for illustration only. Our forecast takes each segment as uniformly bright, at IceCube’s measured flux and spectral index [ 5 ]. In every segment and in the extragalactic flux, the sources make their neutrinos by pion decay. See the text for details. The inner segment, the brightest, is measured best.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Forecast measurements and posterior constraints of the high-energy neutrino flavor composition at Earth across three Galactic plane longitude segments ($|b| < 5^{\circ}$) and the extragalactic diffuse flux, assuming production via pion decay and accounting for full systematic uncertainties.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates double high-energy transients produced by black hole-star binary encounters with massive black holes, offering concrete accretion signatures and event rate predictions for nuclear transients.
analysis.result: The $\mu$TDE produces two accretion flares: a prompt fallback onto the stellar BH with peak rate $\approx 0.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{day}^{-1}$ (duration of hours to days) and a delayed slower return onto the MBH peaking at $\approx 50\,\mathrm{days}$ with a rate $\sim 3$ orders of magnitude lower. The dual-flare event rate is $\Gamma_{2\rm F} \approx 10^{-3}\Gamma_{\rm TDE} \approx 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ at $M_\bullet = 10^6\,M_\odot$, and the time delay follows $\log_{10}(\Delta t_{\rm delay}/{\rm yr}) = 0.2511 - 0.1181X_M + 2.0696X_a + 0.0353X_M^2 + 0.1251X_a^2 - 0.1473X_M X_a$ with $X_M \equiv \log_{10}(M_\bullet/M_\odot)$ and $X_a \equiv \log_{10}(a_{\rm bin}/{\rm AU})$.

analysis.problem: How tidal perturbations from an MBH on a stellar-mass black hole-star binary pump inner binary eccentricity to trigger a micro-TDE and subsequent dual-accretor flares.
analysis.method: High-precision few-body regularized chain scattering simulations using SpaceHub with up to 2.5PN corrections across grids of $M_\bullet$, $a_{\rm bin} \in [0.03, 30]\,\mathrm{AU}$, and $\tilde{v} \equiv v_\infty/v_{\rm orb}$, coupled with loss-cone flux integration ${\cal F}(r)=[{\cal F}_{\rm diff}^{-1}(r)+{\cal F}_{\rm full}^{-1}(r)]^{-1}$ where ${\cal F}_{\rm diff}\approx[\ln(2/\theta_{\rm lc})t_{r}]^{-1}$ and ${\cal F}_{\rm full}\approx\theta_{\rm lc}^{2}/t_{d}$.

analysis.research_progress: Establishes the branching ratios and ballistic debris partition of MBH-induced $\mu$TDEs, deriving the quantitative dual-flare time delay scaling and predicting a single-galaxy rate scaling as $\Gamma_{2\rm F} \propto (M_\bullet/10^8\,M_\odot)^{-(0.8\text{--}1.03)}$.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Snapshot of the spatial (left) and specific-energy (top right) distributions of the $10^{4}$ debris particles at $t=+260.58\,\rm days$ ($\approx 8.56\,\rm months$) after the $\mu$ TDE. The MBH sits at the center of the left panel (big black dot), and the stellar-mass BH companion (small black dot) is seen receding toward the right after its pericenter passage. The colorbar shows the specific energy of each debris particle normalized to the energy spread at the moment of disruption, $\Delta\varepsilon_{\rm frozen}\equiv GM_{\rm BH}R_{\star}/R_{t}^{2}$: blue for debris bound to the MBH ($\varepsilon_{\bullet} 0$). The zoomed-in inset in the left panel shows the debris orbital distribution and the mini-disk bound to the escaping BH. Finally, the lower right panel shows the fallback rates onto the BH and the MBH computed with the direct integration method (solid) and the frozen-in approximation (dashed). An animated version of this figure is available in the online article and at https://youtu.be/g8_UbibAqKQ. The 19 s animation follows the debris from the moment of disruption to $t=+260.58\,\rm days$, showing the formation of the mini-disk around the receding BH and the return of the MBH-bound debris.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Demonstrates the physical mechanism of the double-transient event: tidal perturbation induces a micro-TDE ($\mu$TDE) around the receding stellar-mass BH forming a bound mini-disk, while the remaining debris bound to the central MBH returns to produce a delayed secondary accretion flare, as quantified by the fallback rates onto both black holes.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Heat map of the time delay $\Delta t_{\rm delay}$ between the $\mu$ TDE and the peak fallback onto the perturber in the $a_{\rm bin}$ – $M_{\bullet}$ parameter space assuming the frozen-in approximation. Marginalization over $e_{\rm bin}$ and $v_{\infty}$ results in a median scatter of $\pm 0.67\,\rm dex$ about the values reported in the colorbar. There are no $\mu$ TDE outcomes in the top left gray region. The lower right magenta region corresponds to relativistic encounters for which the binary’s center of mass comes within $100\,R_{g}$ and our Newtonian integration scheme for the debris becomes inadequate.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Maps the theoretical parameter space of the time delay $\Delta t_{\rm delay}$ between the initial $\mu$TDE flare and the peak MBH fallback accretion flare across binary semi-major axis $a_{\rm bin}$ and MBH mass $M_\bullet$, delimiting the physical regimes of $\mu$TDE occurrence and relativistic boundaries.

analysis.result: The radius-scaled shear mode frequencies $f_{s_i} R$ and mass-scaled interface mode frequencies $f_{i_i} M$ follow empirical universal relations parameterized by compactness $\chi \equiv (M/1.4M_\odot)/(R/12\ \mathrm{km})$, $K_0$, and $L$, largely independent of core equation of state stiffness. Spherical and cylindrical phases yield shear frequencies $f_s^{(\mathrm{SpCy})} \gtrsim 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$, while interface modes fall around $10-100\ \mathrm{Hz}$ with gravitational wave damping timescales $\tau_{\rm gw} \gtrsim 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ for $s_1$ and $\tau_{\rm gw} > 10^8\ \mathrm{s}$ for $i_1$.
analysis.problem: Constraining uncertain nuclear matter parameters at saturation—namely incompressibility $K_0$ and symmetry energy slope $L$—using polar crustal oscillations ($s$- and $i$-modes) that penetrate into the stellar core, overcoming the limitation of torsional modes confined strictly to the crust.
analysis.method: Solves linear polar perturbations in a relativistic spherically symmetric metric $ds^{2}=-e^{2\Phi}dt^{2}+(1-2m(r)/r)^{-1}dr^{2}+r^{2}(d\theta^{2}+\sin^{2}\theta d\phi^{2})$ using the Cowling approximation $\delta(\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu})=0$. The crust employs the Oyamatsu-Iida EOS parameterized by $w=w_{0}+\frac{K_{0}}{2}u^{2}+[S_{0}+Lu]\delta^{2}$ with bcc lattice shear modulus $\mu_{\rm sp}=0.1194 n_{i}(Ze)^{2}/a$ and slab phase $\mu_{\rm sl}=0$, while the core uses a parameterized sound-speed EOS $p=\alpha(\varepsilon-\varepsilon_{t})+p_{t}$ with $\alpha=c_s^2$.

analysis.reason: The paper reports phase-resolved X-ray polarimetry of the persistent black hole binary LMC X-1 with IXPE, detecting low-energy orbital modulation and enhanced polarization at inferior conjunction that constrains disk-outflow geometries.
analysis.result: Phase-resolved IXPE polarimetry reveals orbital modulation statistically preferred over a constant model in the $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=10.0, p=0.0004$) and $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=7.53, p=0.0016$) bands, despite an orbit-averaged polarization degree of $\mathrm{PD} = (0.8 \pm 0.4)\%$ below $\mathrm{MDP}_{99} = 1.2\%$. At inferior conjunction ($\\phi \in [-0.1, 0.1]$), polarization increases significantly to $\mathrm{PD} = (3.4 \pm 0.8)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (50 \pm 7)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $\mathrm{PD} = (4.2 \pm 1.1)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (46 \pm 8)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$, aligned with the ionization cone and jet axis ($\sim 45^\circ$). Dilution analysis using $P = P_{\mathrm{disk}} \times (F_{\mathrm{disk}} / F_{\mathrm{total}})$ yields intrinsic disk polarization of $P_{\mathrm{disk}} = (4.6 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $(2.3 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $3\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$.
analysis.problem: Standard electron scattering in an optically thick accretion disk atmosphere with inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$ predicts $\mathrm{PD} \sim 1.3\%$ oriented perpendicular to the disk normal ($\\mathrm{PA} \sim 135^\circ$). This fails to explain the observed enhanced polarization degree $\mathrm{PD} \sim 4\%$ parallel to the disk normal and ionization cone ($\\mathrm{PA} \approx 46^\circ$) at inferior conjunction, as well as the significant orbital phase modulation.
analysis.method: Coordinated timing, spectral, and polarimetric data reduction of IXPE ($2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 562\,\mathrm{ks}$), NICER ($1\text{--}10\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 25\,\mathrm{ks}$), and NuSTAR ($3\text{--}40\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 19\,\mathrm{ks}$) folded at $P = 3.90917\,\mathrm{days}$. Stokes parameter variations were fitted using $(Q/I)(t) = A_Q \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0)) + C_Q$ and $(U/I)(t) = A_U \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0) - \pi) + C_U$. Instrument cross-calibration was handled via the $\mathrm{MBPO}$ broken power-law model, and spectro-polarimetry used $\mathrm{MBPO} \times \mathrm{TBABS} \times (\mathrm{KERRBB} + \mathrm{NTHCOMP} + \mathrm{GAUSS})$.
assumptions: The binary parameters are fixed to black hole mass $M_{\mathrm{BH}} = (10.9 \pm 1.4)\,M_\odot$, companion mass $(32 \pm 3)\,M_\odot$, and orbital inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents 1D and 2D PIC simulations demonstrating that magnetic reconnection in shock-compressed Alfvén wave trains preferentially heats ions over electrons ($E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.4$), providing important microphysical constraints on collisionless shock energy partitioning.
analysis.result: In 2D parallel shocks, magnetic reconnection occurring in downstream compressed Alfvénic current sheets strongly heats ions, driving the electron-to-ion kinetic energy density ratio from $E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.7\text{--}0.9$ in 1D down to $E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.4$ ($E_{\rm ion}/E_0 \sim 2.8$ and $E_{\rm ele}/E_0 \sim 1.15$ for $u_0 = 0.4$). Preferential ion heating saturates when the transverse domain width exceeds $Y/(c/\omega_{\rm pi}) > 1.57$, whereas at low magnetization and high Mach numbers (e.g., $\sigma < 4\times 10^{-3}$ with $M_A \sim 5.9$ at $u_0 = 0.4$), reconnection heating becomes negligible and yields $E_e/E_i \sim 0.2\text{--}0.35$ in both 1D and 2D.

analysis.problem: How magnetic reconnection and large-amplitude Alfvén waves in collisionless parallel shocks govern electron versus ion energy partitioning ($E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion}$) and resolve the discrepancies between 1D and multi-dimensional shock heating.
analysis.method: 1D and 2D kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of parallel collisionless shocks ($u_0 = 0.4$ and $0.2$, $\sigma = B_0^2/[4\pi n_0(m_i+m_e)\gamma_0 c^2] = 0.0158$, $M_A = (u_0/\gamma_0)/\sqrt{\sigma/(\sigma+1)} \sim 3.06$, $m_i/m_e = 100$, $c/\omega_{\rm pi} = 230$ grid cells, transverse size $L_y = 26 c/\omega_{\rm pi}$), isolating 1D wave-particle resonances (ion-cyclotron resonance $\omega = kV_b - \Omega_{\rm ci}$, electron cyclotron absorption $\omega + kv_{\rm ele} = \Omega_{\rm ce}/\gamma_e$) and comparing with 2D magnetic reconnection in compressed turbulent current sheets.
assumptions: Reduced ion-to-electron mass ratio of $m_i/m_e = 100$ under parallel background magnetic field $\vec{B} = (B_0, 0, 0)$.
limits: Reconnection-driven preferential ion heating becomes negligible in weakly magnetized, high-Mach shocks (e.g., $\sigma < 4\times 10^{-3}$, $M_A \sim 5.9$).

Purple arrowheads indicate the direction of flow on the contours of the vacated region due to the missing vortices. analysis.reason: This paper presents a multi-year low-frequency (102-198 MHz) study of Crab giant pulses using I-LOFAR, investigating the dynamic correlation between dispersion measure (DM) and scattering timescales as probes of plasma turbulence in the Crab Nebula.
analysis.result: Dispersive delay scales as $\Delta t \propto \mathrm{DM}\,\nu^{-2}$ across the $102.23\text{--}197.55\text{ MHz}$ band, alongside scattering broadening $\tau(f) = \tau_{150}[f/150~\mathrm{MHz}]^\alpha$. Measured $\mathrm{DM}$ and $\tau$ exhibit strong positive correlation ($r = 0.71 \pm 0.04$, $\rho = 0.78 \pm 0.04$ for the thin screen model), peaking at $r \approx 0.48\text{--}0.49$ after removing long-term trends at a sliding window of $W \approx 125\text{--}190~\mathrm{d}$ with zero lag, alongside an isolated nebula filament crossing event with $\Delta\mathrm{DM} \approx 0.02~\mathrm{pc~cm^{-3}}$.
analysis.problem: Low-frequency radio timing and DM determination of giant pulses are severely degenerated by intense scattering broadening, while solar wind electron density fluctuations ($n \propto r^{-2}$) are masked by large intrinsic DM variations within the Crab Nebula.
analysis.method: Giant pulse searching was conducted via TransientX on 8-bit filterbanks, followed by coherent metric optimization with DM_phase maximizing $S(\mathrm{DM}) = \sum_f w(f) P(f;\mathrm{DM})$ on phase-normalized spectra, and scattering tail fitting across $9.53~\mathrm{MHz}$ subbands using modified thin-screen and thick-screen models evaluated by the Akaike Information Criterion.
assumptions: Dispersive pulse delay scales strictly as $\Delta t \propto \nu^{-2}$ while the scattering timescale across subbands follows $\tau(f) \propto f^\alpha$.
limits: Scattering pulse broadening at low frequencies induces apparent DM shifts and limits single giant pulse DM precision, while Crab Nebula intrinsic DM variations exceed the solar wind signal ($10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-4}~\mathrm{pc~cm^{-3}}$).
citation_leads: 3.2 Identifying Pulses: “To reduce computational cost, the search was performed on 8-bit filterbanks rather than 32-bit.”

3.3 Correcting the DM: “Due to the large amount of scattering present at lower frequencies, traditional boxcar single-pulse searches can often over or underestimate the DM as they simply maximise S/N over a reasonably coarse search grid in DM and pulse width.”

4.3 Scattering: “The lower the observing frequency, the smaller the DM uncertainty, since the dispersive delay across a fixed bandwidth scales as $\sim f^{-2}$, in theory improving the accuracy of the determined DM.”
4.5 Implications on the Solar Wind: “The variations in DM caused by the Crab Nebula are too large to measure temporal variations in electron content caused by the solar wind.”
analysis.research_progress: Constrained multi-year co-evolution of $\mathrm{DM}$ and scattering $\tau$ on month-scale baselines for Crab giant pulses at metric wavelengths, and established limits on disentangling turbulent nebula filament crossings from solar wind variations.

analysis.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch spectropolarimetry and 3D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of the Type Ibn supernova SN 2025kzr, offering constraints on circumstellar interaction geometry and ejecta-CSM alignment.
analysis.result: The optical spectrum displays $\mathrm{He\ I}$ emission with $\mathrm{FWHM} \sim 1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, confirming strong ejecta-CSM interaction. After subtracting the interstellar polarization ($Q_{\mathrm{ISP}} = 0.154\% \pm 0.145\%, U_{\mathrm{ISP}} = 0.396\% \pm 0.173\%$, $P_{\mathrm{ISP}} \approx 0.43\%$, $\theta_{\mathrm{ISP}} \approx 34^\circ$), the intrinsic continuum polarization reaches $P = 0.462\% \pm 0.071\%$ at $+8.0\ \mathrm{d}$ with $(Q_{\mathrm{Cont}}, U_{\mathrm{Cont}}) = (0.242\% \pm 0.076\%, -0.394\% \pm 0.067\%)$, subsequently declining to $P = 0.042\% \pm 0.071\%$ at $+12\ \mathrm{d}$ and consistent with zero by $+21\ \mathrm{d}$. The polarization vector traces an evolving loop in the $Q-U$ plane: from near zero at $4.9\ \mathrm{d}$ to $(Q, U) \approx (0.21\%, -0.34\%)$ at $8.0\ \mathrm{d}$, rotating to $(0.49\%, 0.32\%)$ at $10.9\ \mathrm{d}$. The $\mathrm{He\ I}\ \lambda 5876$ line polarization aligns with a dominant axis angle $\theta_{\mathrm{DA}} = (-45.6^{+15.6}_{-15.5})^\circ$. The polarization trajectory is reproduced by an interaction between a prolate ejecta ($A_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.25, \theta_{\mathrm{ej}} = +8^\circ$) and an oblate CSM ($A_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 1.20, \theta_{\mathrm{CSM}} = -25^\circ$) accompanied by anisotropic surface luminance $L_{\mathrm{iso}}/L_{\mathrm{iso,max}}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2. Hydrodynamic Model and Q − U Evolution
analysis.problem: Unraveling the multi-dimensional geometry and alignment of the dense helium-rich CSM and supernova ejecta in Type Ibn SN 2025kzr, breaking the geometric degeneracies inherent to 1D light curve models (e.g., $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}} \propto r^{-3}$) and flux spectra.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch spectropolarimetry using VLT/FORS2 (300V grism, $3500\text{--}9200\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$, $R \approx 440$) at $+8.0, +25.0, +34.0\ \mathrm{d}$ combined with $V$-band imaging polarimetry across 5–34 days. ISP was determined from late-time iron-group element phases. 3D gray radiation-hydrodynamics simulations were performed using Athena++ for a broken power-law prolate ejecta ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.85\ M_\odot, E_{\mathrm{kin}} = 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}, \delta=1, m=10, v_{\mathrm{br}} = 8.81 \times 10^8\ \mathrm{cm\ s^{-1}}$) colliding with an oblate broken-density CSM ($s_1=0.5, s_2=30, s_3=2$), followed by 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer in MCPol tracking $2 \times 10^6$ photon packets.
assumptions: The CSM is modeled as an oblate ellipsoid with axial ratio $A_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 1.20$, while the SN ejecta is modeled as a prolate ellipsoid with $A_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.25$.
limits: Smooth axisymmetric ellipsoidal geometries with post-processed electron scattering introduce parameter degeneracies among geometry, viewing angle, optical depth, and ISP.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Time-variable ejecta-CSM geometry and the model continuum polarization. Panel A: Schematic of the interaction region that spans the transition from CSM-interaction-dominated to CDS-dominated phases (see Section III.2 ) as seen perpendicular to the $x$ – $z$ plane. At $\sim$ 0–6 d, the forward shock (solid red) is embedded in the optically thick, oblate CSM (blue) and lies inside the $\tau=1$ surface (dashed orange). At $\sim$ 7–11 d, the forward shock approaches the outer, optically thinner part of the dense CSM. After $\sim$ 11 d, the shock has swept through the dense CSM, the CDS has formed between the forward and reverse shocks, and the $\tau=1$ surface lies within the CDS at some angles. The long axes of the prolate SN ejecta (red arrow) and the oblate CSM (blue arrow) are misaligned, with inclinations $\theta_{\rm ej}$ and $\theta_{\rm CSM}$ (Section IV ). The schematic is not to scale. Panel B: Model continuum polarization $P$ of the oblate, CSM-dominated phase as a function of the axis ratio $A_{\rm oblate}=a/c$, where $a$ and $c$ are the equatorial and polar semiaxes. Blue, orange, and green dashed curves show photon packets injected at electron-scattering optical depths of $\tau=1$, 2, and 3, respectively. Gray-shaded band shows the observed, ISP-corrected and bias-corrected polarization and its $1\sigma$ uncertainty at 4.9 d and 8d, respectively. Panel C: Same as Panel B but for the prolate, CDS-dominated phase as a function of $A_{\rm prolate}=c/a$, compared with the observation at 10.9 d. Panels B and C show that polarization increases with asphericity and decreases with injection depth.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Presents the geometric framework of the interaction region across the transition from an oblate CSM-dominated phase to a prolate CDS-dominated phase with misaligned symmetry axes ($\theta_{\rm ej}$ and $\theta_{\rm CSM}$), alongside theoretical continuum polarization curves $P$ modeled as functions of axis ratios ($A_{\rm oblate}=a/c$, $A_{\rm prolate}=c/a$) and electron-scattering optical depth $\tau = 1, 2, 3$.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Hydrodynamic structure, emitting-surface brightness, and polarization evolution of the model at 5, 8, and 11 d. Panel A: Density maps in the $x$ – $z$ plane. Colors show $\log_{10}(\rho/\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}})$. The dark-green solid, yellow dashed, and blue dash-dotted curves denote the forward shock, the $\tau=1$ surface, and the $\rho=10^{-16}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ contour tracing the CSM geometry, respectively. Panel B: Normalized brightness distributions of the emitting surfaces viewed from the $-y$ direction. The 5 d surface is the shock surface, whereas the 8 and 11 d surfaces are defined by $\tau=1$. Colors indicate $L_{\rm iso}/L_{\rm iso,max}$, normalized independently at each epoch. Panel C: Comparison between the modeled and ISP-corrected observed Stokes parameters in the $Q-U$ plane. Colored diamonds show the $+y$ model predictions at 5, 8, and 11 d; open circles present the observations at 4.9, 8.0, and 10.9 d. The black solid curve connects the model epochs, and dotted segments illustrate the model–observation offsets. Error bars indicate $1\sigma$ uncertainties, including Monte Carlo uncertainties for the model and measurement uncertainties for the observations.
figures.label: Fig. 4

The flavor survival probability asymptotically tends to flavor equipartition $P_{ee} = \frac{1}{2}(P_{0}+P_{3})/P_{0} \simeq \frac{1}{2}(1+\|\bm{P}\|/P_{0})$ governed by polarization vector decoherence $\mathrm{d}_{t}\|\bm{P}\|^{2} \propto -R_{\mathrm{EA}}|\rho_{ex}|^{2} \propto -R_{\mathrm{EA}}/(1+R_{\mathrm{EA}}^{2})$, while collisional decoherence suppresses spatial cascading and prevents strong spatial inhomogeneity.

analysis.reason: This work directly addresses the progenitor channels of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by testing whether FRBs track cosmic star formation history promptly or with a multi-gigayear delay time distribution.
analysis.result: When marginalizing over fluence calibration systematics and fitting the dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}$) distribution alone, both CHIME catalogs reveal a significant cosmological time delay: Catalog 1 yields $t_{d}=3.90^{+0.50}_{-0.41}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.99^{+0.01}_{-0.24}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, while Catalog 2 yields $t_{d}=3.53^{+0.11}_{-0.10}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.82^{+0.15}_{-0.14}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, resolving the apparent $t_d \sim 0$ result that arises from instrumental $\mathrm{S/N}$--fluence mapping biases.
analysis.problem: Whether FRB occurrence rates follow prompt core-collapse supernova magnetar channels or delayed compact binary mergers, and how systematic uncertainties in telescope beam attenuation and fluence threshold mapping bias delay time inference in forward modeling.
analysis.method: Forward modeling using a two-dimensional binning scheme over $\mathrm{S/N}$ and $\mathrm{DM}$ with synthetic injection samples, Poisson likelihood $\ln\mathcal{L}\propto\sum_{i,j}[n_{ij}\ln\zeta_{ij}-\zeta_{ij}]$, and an intrinsic burst energy distribution parameterized by a Schechter function $P(E)\propto\frac{1}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\left(\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)^{\gamma}\exp\left(-\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)$ convolved with cosmic SFR and Gaussian DTD.
assumptions: The intrinsic energy distribution of FRBs follows a Schechter function characterized by a power-law slope $\gamma$ and an exponential cutoff at characteristic energy $E_{\mathrm{char}}$.
citation_leads: IV.2 The Effect of S/N: “For Catalog 1, we obtain a delay time of $t_{d}=3.90^{+0.50}_{-0.41}$ Gyr with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.99^{+0.01}_{-0.24}$ Gyr.”
II.1 Two-dimensional binning scheme: “To compare the model predictions with the observed data, we construct a two-dimensional histogram of the observed S/N and DM.”
Appendix B Fluence distribution: “We model the intrinsic energy distribution of FRBs with a Schechter function, characterized by a power-law slope $\gamma$”

analysis.problem: Investigating whether high-redshift radio-quiet ($R < 10$) QSOs genuinely lack relativistic jets or if traditional radio loudness criteria fail due to Doppler de-beaming and suppressed extended lobe emission in the early Universe.
analysis.method: Cross-matching $808$ optically confirmed $z \ge 4$ QSOs with ASKAP EMU survey data at $0.943\,\mathrm{GHz}$ using a $6.4''$ positional tolerance. limits: The $\sim 15''$ angular resolution of EMU corresponds to $\sim 80\text{--}100\,\mathrm{kpc}$ at $z=4\text{--}6.6$, leaving sources unresolved and preventing morphological separation of cores and extended lobes without VLBI.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a large-scale statistical identification and multi-frequency geometric modeling of 586 curved parsec-scale relativistic jets in AGN, providing systematic observational constraints on relativistic jet propagation, precession mechanisms, and supermassive black hole binary or accretion disc dynamics.
analysis.result: Among 7,927 resolved AGN sources, 586 show reliable curvature with bending rate $|K|$ increasing at higher frequencies, tracing stronger deflection in the innermost jet. Linear helical modeling gives a mean curvature $K^{-1}_{\rm mean} = 109^{\circ}/{\rm mas}$, corresponding to inferred precession periods $P \sim 10\text{--}10^{4}~{\rm yr}$ (logarithmic mean $218.8~{\rm yr}$). For binary black hole models, disk tidal precession $P_{\rm td} \approx 6.5 \times 10^{2} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{3} (R_{d}/10^{4} r_{g})^{-3/2}~{\rm yr}$ matches observations much better than spin geodetic precession $P_{\rm geo} \approx 2.6 \times 10^{8} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{5/2}~{\rm yr}$, while tilted thick disc Lense-Thirring precession $P_{\rm BH, spin, thick} \approx 24.7 s^{-1} M_{8} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{g})^{3} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{\rm i})^{1/2}~{\rm yr}$ naturally reproduces the observed range of $10^{1\text{--}5}~{\rm yr}$.
analysis.problem: Determining the physical origins of parsec-scale relativistic jet bending in active galaxies, specifically distinguishing between geometric precession (induced by supermassive binary black hole orbits or Bardeen-Petterson/Lense-Thirring disc warping) and plasma dynamical instabilities (Kelvin-Helmholtz helical modes).
analysis.method: Filtered 123,456 Astrogeo VLBI images (1.2–86 GHz) down to 63,879 images of 7,927 resolved sources using 2D Gaussian subtraction with threshold $\sigma_{\rm crit} = 5.5\sigma_{\rm map}$. Identified curved jets via median ridge lines with $\Delta\phi = |K|(r_{\rm max} - r_{\rm min}) > 20^{\circ}$, then performed gradient-free global optimization fitting to linear helices (scaling parameter $K = \frac{1}{\pi}\frac{c}{d}\frac{\beta}{1-\beta}P\sin\psi$) and logarithmic helices ($K_{\rm log} = \frac{2\pi}{\tan\psi}[\frac{r_0}{\lambda_0}]$), inverting physical parameters through $10^4$ Monte Carlo draws from empirical prior distributions.
assumptions: Jet nozzle precession can be directly coupled to either binary orbital perturbations or the spin and warping of the accretion disc.
limits: The linear criterion $|\Delta\phi| > 20^{\circ}$ selectively identifies large-scale steady bending while being insensitive to short-wavelength wiggles or small-scale oscillatory perturbations.

analysis.reason: J1912-4410 is only the second known white dwarf pulsar, providing a critical laboratory to test compact object spin-down power and magnetospheric non-thermal emission mechanisms. Measuring its spin-down rate directly tests whether the system is purely rotationally powered or aided by accretion.
analysis.problem: Determining whether the multi-wavelength pulsed non-thermal emission of the white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410 is powered solely by rotational spin-down or assisted by accretion, and testing the viability of the unipolar synchronar magnetospheric interaction model.
analysis.method: Multi-band ($u, g, r, i$) high-speed time-series photometry obtained with ULTRACAM over 28 nights was reduced with HiPERCAM. Pulse arrival times were derived via cross-correlation with a Gaussian template (optimal width $\sigma = 29.3\,\mathrm{s}$ in $g$). Orbital modulation and timing residuals were disentangled using a 10-term Fourier series and iteratively fitted to a quadratic ephemeris $T_{\rm max} = T_0 + P_{\rm spin} E + \frac{1}{2} P_{\rm spin} \dot{P}_{\rm spin} E^2$ with MCMC parameter estimation.
limits: Pulse arrival times in the $i$-band deviate from the consistent $u, g, r$ ephemeris, possibly due to filter-dependent emission heights or chromatic phase offsets
citation_leads: Determining the Spin-down of the White Dwarf in J191213.72-441045.1 using Optical Time-Series Photometry: “J191213.72-441045.1 (J1912-4410) is the second white dwarf pulsar to be discovered.”
3 Data Analysis: “Data points flagged by the HiPERCAM reduction pipeline as having bad counts”
4.2 Compatibility with the Synchronar Model: “From this, we obtain a minimum WD magnetic field strength of $110\pm 50$”
4.4 $i$-Filter Photometry: “the arrival times of pulses for J1912-4410 vary depending on the filter being used for observations.”
analysis.research_progress: Provides the first robust measurement of the spin-down rate $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = 4.13(8) \times 10^{-12}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and spin-down luminosity $\dot{E}_{\rm rot} = 9^{+6}_{-5} \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{W}$ for the second white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410, showing that WD pulsars are a heterogeneous class and conclusively ruling out the synchronar model ($B \ge 110 \pm 50\,\mathrm{MG}$ vs. empirical upper limit $B \lesssim 50\,\mathrm{MG}$).

figures.caption: Figure 1: Lightcurve of J1912-4410 in the optical $u$ (top), $g$ (middle) and $i$ (bottom) bandpasses where the WD pulsar shows clear pulsed and periodic emission which is modulated by the spin frequency. Here, we plot the relative flux divided by the median flux of the observation night.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Multi-band optical light curves ($u$, $g$, and $i$) of J1912-4410 exhibiting rapid, periodic pulsed emission directly modulated by the white dwarf spin frequency.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Residuals plot (observed minus calculated, O–C) of pulse arrival times after the linear ephemeris is subtracted and the residuals in Fig. 3 are corrected for using $g$ filter data. The grey data points display the raw data. We also bin the data according to the night of observation; the black data points display the mean O–C of each bin, with the error calculated from the standard error within each bin. The quadratic fit is plotted as a dashed line. Different years of observation are highlighted by alternating red and white background columns, with the years marked on top.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: Pulse arrival time $(O-C)$ residuals spanning four years after subtracting the linear ephemeris and orbital modulation, fitted with a quadratic ephemeris to measure the spin-down rate $\dot{P} = 4.13(8) \times 10^{-12}\text{ s s}^{-1}$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents observational sensitivity forecasts and theoretical frameworks for measuring the flavor composition of Galactic and extragalactic high-energy neutrinos using eight neutrino telescopes, enabling tests of cosmic-ray hadronic production mechanisms, source magnetic fields, and neutrino decay.
analysis.result: With eight neutrino telescopes, the source electron flavor fraction $f_{e,{\rm S}}$ for the inner Galactic plane can be measured to $27\%$ precision at $68\%$ C.L., distinguishing pion decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1/3$) from muon damping ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=0$) and neutron decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1$) at $>95\%$ C.L. In extragalactic sources, muon synchrotron cooling above $E_{c} \approx E_{c,\mu}/3$ with $E_{c,\mu} \simeq 6\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$ can be detected at $\ge 3\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 11\text{ kG}$ ($5\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 22\text{ kG}$), while neutrino invisible decay lifetime-to-mass ratio can be probed up to $\tau/m \sim 1.5\times 10^4\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ at $2\sigma$.
analysis.reading_entry: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
analysis.problem: High-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way have an unknown flavor composition $(f_{e}, f_{\mu}, f_{\tau})$ and production origin (diffuse interstellar $pp$ collisions versus unresolved discrete sources), and existing facilities lack the sensitivity to distinguish emission mechanisms, detect muon synchrotron cooling in magnetized environments, or constrain neutrino decay against extragalactic baselines.
analysis.method: The analysis uses a frequentist profile likelihood method based on Poisson event rates and Wilks' theorem across eight neutrino telescopes (IceCube, KM3NeT/ARCA, Baikal-GVD, P-ONE, TRIDENT, NEON, HUNT, IceCube-Gen2). The framework models detector tracks and cascades, computes atmospheric backgrounds using MCEq with Sibyll-2.3d and nuVeto self-veto, incorporates muon synchrotron cooling with critical cutoff $E_{c} \simeq 2\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$, and folds in standard averaged neutrino oscillations $f_{\beta,\oplus} = \sum_{\alpha} P_{\alpha\beta} f_{\alpha,{\rm S}}$.
assumptions: Neutrinos in standard hadronuclear environments are produced via charged pion decay chains giving source flavor ratios $(f_{e,{\rm S}}, f_{\mu,{\rm S}}, f_{\tau,{\rm S}}) = (1/3, 2/3, 0)$ without initial tau neutrinos.
limits: Muon synchrotron cooling produces observable spectral/flavor suppression only in magnetized environments with $B \gtrsim 10^4\text{ G}$ where $E_c \lesssim 100\text{ TeV}$.
citation_leads: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way: “The significance with which the fractions are told apart grows in proportion to their difference, whatever their values.”
Appendix A Cooling in the extragalactic sources: “A muon in a magnetic field $B$ loses energy by synchrotron radiation faster than it decays above the energy”
analysis.research_progress: The study demonstrates that multi-telescope arrays scale flavor discrimination significance linearly with fraction difference $|\Delta f_{e,{\rm S}}|$, improving the constraint on Galactic $f_{e,{\rm S}}$ from $88\%$ with current facilities to $27\%$, breaking degeneracies between pion decay and muon-damped regimes, and extending neutrino decay limits by over an order of magnitude.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Flavor composition of the high-energy neutrinos along the Galactic plane and from outside it. Forecast measurements of the composition at Earth in IceCube’s three segments of the plane and of the extragalactic flux, all fitted together with every systematic uncertainty. The segments span ranges of Galactic longitude, $l$, at Galactic latitudes $|b| [ 9 ] for illustration only. Our forecast takes each segment as uniformly bright, at IceCube’s measured flux and spectral index [ 5 ]. In every segment and in the extragalactic flux, the sources make their neutrinos by pion decay. See the text for details. The inner segment, the brightest, is measured best.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Forecast measurements and posterior constraints of the high-energy neutrino flavor composition at Earth across three Galactic plane longitude segments ($|b| < 5^{\circ}$) and the extragalactic diffuse flux, assuming production via pion decay and accounting for full systematic uncertainties.
